 ⚽ Europa League updates, kicking off from 5.45pm GMT
 ⚽ Live scores | Europa League table | And email Simon

Photograph: David Klein/Reuters Simon Burnton (now) and Will Unwin (later) Thu 5 Nov 2026 13.35 EST First published on Thu 5 Nov 2026 11.15 EST Share Key events 3m ago GOAL! Thun 2-0 Hearts (Labeau, 34 mins) 
 9m ago Sparta go down to 10 men! 
 11m ago GOAL! Sparta Prague 1-0 Bournemouth (Singhateh, 35 mins) 
 22m ago GOAL! Thun 1-0 Hearts (McCart own goal, 22 mins) 
 38m ago GOAL! Crystal Palace 0-1 Hoffenheim (Prass, 7 mins) 
 2h ago (A selection of) team news! 
 2h ago Preamble 
 now 13.35 EST It’s half-time at Selhurst Park, where Hoffenheim have nursed their 1-0 lead into the break. It’s a popular scoreline tonight: tt is currently 1-0 in six of the eight Europa League games, and 0-0 in the other two.
 Share 3m ago 13.32 EST GOAL! Thun 2-0 Hearts (Labeau, 34 mins)
 A goal and an assist now for Hearts defenders! It’s a lightning counter-attack from the Swiss which ends with a low cross from the right, and an attempt to clear that only sent the ball rolling to Brighton Labeau, maybe eight yards out, who slams it into the net!
 Share 9m ago 13.25 EST Sparta go down to 10 men!
 Moments later, they’re down to 10! It was a ludicrous challenge from Tobias Guddal, not even remotely violent, but very deliberate and entirely off the ball, and it inevitably earns him a second yellow card!
 Share 11m ago 13.23 EST GOAL! Sparta Prague 1-0 Bournemouth (Singhateh, 35 mins)
 Jakub Surovcik, the Sparta goalkeeper, catches a Bournemouth corner and bowls it out to Ebrima Singhateh, and he does the rest! It’s an excellent run, but when it was one against three on the edge of the Bournemouth defence the chances of him scoring didn’t look great. But somehow he beat them all, ran clear, and finished beautifully!
 View image in fullscreen Ebrima Singhateh gives Sparta Prague the lead over the Cherries. Photograph: Kieran McManus/Shutterstock Share Updated at  13.29 EST 16m ago 13.19 EST And I rather underplayed that Hearts own goal. McCart was about 14 yards out, and got a bit of a push in the back from the forward he was racing, but he then got his feet in a muddle and, off balance, scuffed the ball into the corner!
 Share 17m ago 13.18 EST Lewis Cook has missed the penalty! He stutters, sends the keeper the wrong way, and sidefoots into the post! The ball ricochets between the prone goalkeeper and his goalline, and away to safety!
 View image in fullscreen Oh Lewis… Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images Share Updated at  13.20 EST 19m ago 13.16 EST Penalty to Bournemouth! The referee has spotted a handball in the Sparta penalty area, and Hoever certainly blocked a cross with something!
 Share 20m ago 13.15 EST Between Freiburg’s goal at Trabzonspor and Anderlecht’s against Salzburg about six minutes passed. Seventeen games were being played across the two European competitions, so that’s around 102 goalless minutes. Which seems unlikely. Anyway, they’re making up for it now! Ajax have scored against Midtylland, and Omonia Nicosia are 1-0 up at NEC.
 Share 22m ago 13.13 EST GOAL! Thun 1-0 Hearts (McCart own goal, 22 mins)
 I’ve seen only the very briefest snippet of this goal, and that from an unhelpful angle, but it was one of those where a defender has to do something with the ball, otherwise an opponent is only going to turn it in. Obviously turning it in themselves is not ideal, but there you go.
 Share 25m ago 13.09 EST A home side has scored! It’s Anderlecht, who have gone one up against Salzburg through Ludwig Augustinsson, and it’s an absolute beauty of a free-kick! From a couple of yards outside the penalty area, he curls it over the wall and the keeper doesn’t even move!
 Share 32m ago 13.02 EST Freiburg go one up at Trabzonspor, a tap-in for Lukas Kubler after Matanovic’s header from a corner comes back off the keeper, and so far 100% of tonight’s goals have been scored by away teams.
 Share 35m ago 13.00 EST A team in blue and red stripes has the ball in the net, but there are no Crystal Palace fans celebrating – because it’s Viktoria Plzen going a goal up at Lillestrom.
 Share 36m ago 12.59 EST Play has meanwhile resumed at Thun, but there will be a good four minutes of smoke-related stoppage time to play before half-time.
 View image in fullscreen Smoke from pyrotechnics interrupts play during the Conference League match between Switzerland's Thun and Scotland's Hearts of Midlothian. Photograph: Anthony Anex/EPA Share 38m ago 12.56 EST GOAL! Crystal Palace 0-1 Hoffenheim (Prass, 7 mins)
 Hoffenheim’s first significant attack, and it’s a good one! They win the ball back at the edge of their D and break fast, first down the right and then with an early crossfield pass to Alexander Prass, sprinting clear from his own half. He hits a hard, low, first-time shot and Dean Henderson takes the sting off it but not the momentum, and it rolls over the line!
 View image in fullscreen Alexander Prass fires Hoffenheim ahead against Crystal Palace. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters View image in fullscreen Photograph: Henry Nicholls/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  13.01 EST 42m ago 12.52 EST Meanwhile Crystal Palace have the ball in the net against Hoffenheim, but Daichi Kamada was well offside.
 Share 44m ago 12.51 EST Fireworks stop play at Thun! There’s no way anyone can play in the amount of smoke that has settled across the pitch in Switzerland.
 Share 45m ago 12.50 EST What a miss! Jonatan Braut Brunes, the Sparta Prague striker, sends the ball squirming just wide of a gaping Bournemouth goal from an admittedly very firm pull-back.
 Share 46m ago 12.48 EST OK, football is now actually happening in all eight early Europa League kick-offs. Milan v Ferencvaros was the last to get going.
 Share 48m ago 12.46 EST Though actually none of the games I’m monitoring have started yet, with delays including the minute’s silence for Jesus de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-pitch collision at the weekend. “Perusing the Sparta Prague team sheet,” writes Peter Oh, “I can’t help but wonder, will the club from the Czech capital be able to stop the Cherries’ run of good form? Mbe Soh. Mbe Soh.”
 Share 50m ago 12.45 EST 5.45pm: Football o’clock!
 Share 53m ago 12.41 EST The players are emerging from their various tunnels, kick-off mere moments away!
 Share 1h ago 12.31 EST Pierre Sage is asked why Axel Disasi is not in the Crystal Palace squad tonight. “It’s a decision I took today.” Is there a reason for that? “No.” Also from Sage:
 double quotation mark We are ready to fight and compete in this game. We need to start a new way, because we need points in every competition, and I think the start of this way is tonight. They are a team who like intensity, sprint a lot, and they play forward, it’s very vertical. But they are able to take control of the play inside too. We have to deal with these two things, and we have to take control first of all today.
 Share 1h ago 12.20 EST Bournemouth’s Marco Rose has a chat about momentum, and his eight changes to the lineup today:
 double quotation mark It’s always about hard work and we have to maintain momentum every day, in every training, and every game, and today it’s getting a tough challenge. Everyone is in a good spot. The lads who played the last weeks showed up. I hope we have fresh legs. There is no other option for me, because Sunday we have the next game and then again and again.
 And on Bournemouth, and the very good place they currently appear to be in:
 double quotation mark It’s always about connections and emotions in football. I really feel the commitment of our fans, of the region. Everyone is so happy after hard times in the 90s. To get this kind of experience, it’s just a joy to be part of it and it makes me proud.
 Share 1h ago 12.05 EST Also today: 
 Read Jeff Rueter’s Champions League review and Barry Glendenning in Football Daily on the might of Como 
 Harry Kane turns his Ballon d’Or into actual gold, or at least a very lucrative new contract 
 53 red cards in one game! Inevitably, it’s in Brazil 
 Share 2h ago 11.55 EST (A selection of) team news!
 Here’s the all-important team news for the three early kick-offs involving British teams:
 Europa League
 Crystal ⁠Palace v Hoffenheim 
 Crystal Palace: Henderson, Canvot, Richards, Ahanor, Khalaili, Timber, Wharton, Mitchell, Kamada, Mateta, Pino. Subs: Benitez, Benetton, Nketiah, McNeil, Larsen, Osorio, Mingueza, Williams, James Kalembo.

 Referee: Horatiu Fesnic (Romania).
 Sparta ‌Prague v Bournemouth
Sparta Prague: Surovcik, Hoever, Mbe Soh, Guddall, Suchomel, Macek, Mannsverk, Irving, Singhateh, Brunes, Alcocer. Subs: Hegyi, Kaderabek, Martinec, Eneme, Vitalyos, Grimaldo, Vydra, Vojta, Zeleny, Jurasek, Sochurek, Dyntar.
 Bournemouth: Di Gregorio, Smith, Hill, Diakite, Soler, Cook, Christie, Adli, Brooks, Doak, Rodriguez. Subs: Petrovic, Allan, Truffert, Evanilson, Adams, Silva, Tavernier, Kluivert, Rayan.
 Referee: Erik Lambrechts (Belgium)
 Conference League

 Thun: Steffen, Dahler, Bamert, Burki, Mambwa, Reichmuth, Kait, Roth, Maier, Dursun, Labeau. Subs: Spycher, Burgy, Zoukit, Kristal, Strannegard, Braschi, Derbaci, Christoffersson, Gutbub, Fehr, Ilic, Lengen.
 Hearts: Reus, Altena, Walcott, Findlay, McCart, Kingsley, Kerjota, Mendy, McPake, Guendouz, Braga. Subs: Clark, Fulton, Williams, Kabore, Wilson, Pollock, Stevenson, Gillies.
 Referee: Kyriakos Athanasiou (Cyprus).
 Share 2h ago 11.48 EST The deluge has arrived! Team news for the British sides on its way. If you have other games you’d like teams from, let me know.
 View image in fullscreen The deluge has arrived! Photograph: Tingshu Wang/Reuters Share 2h ago 11.34 EST I’ve donned my Mac and raised my brolly in preparation for a deluge of team news. In the meantime, here’s a photo of what looks a fine evening in Prague.
 View image in fullscreen A general view of the epet Arena, where Sparta Prague play Bournemouth in the Europa League. Photograph: Kieran McManus/Shutterstock Share 2h ago 11.15 EST Preamble
 Hello world! Another day, another smorgasbord of European delights is being plated up for our delectation tonight. There are, to summarise, too many games going on simultaneously for two eyes to have any hope of following but I’ll do my very best.
 Highlights? Well [he writes, copy-and-pasting the preview filed by the Associated Press] , Bournemouth travel to Sparta Prague in the Europa League with the aim to stay perfect after four rounds. The English side has been cruising in its maiden European campaign with three wins over Milan, Sturm Graz and Real Sociedad. Bournemouth have also surged to eighth in the Premier League after another three straight wins. “We need to be very reasonable, we know that it’s a long way and I especially know it,” winger Amine Adli, who reached the 2024 Europa League final with Leverkusen, said ahead of the match in Prague. “It’s a long way to the final.”
 His former employers also have a 100% record and host pointless Marseille. Milan plays another undefeated club, Ferencvaros, at San Siro, and another Italian giant, Juventus, visit Alkmaar. Struggling Crystal Palace welcome Hoffenheim and Celtic, one of four teams yet to earn a single point, host Besiktas in Glasgow.
 In the Conference League, Brighton face Getafe away, while Monaco, up against Danish side Nordsjælland, have been boosted by signing US striker Folarin Balogun.
